speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; these are concerning systemic symptoms. To begin our investigation, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or stool color regarding your abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The worsening abdominal pain and significant weight loss are concerning; have you noticed any blood in your stool or changes in your appetite recently? Additionally, do you have any history of recent travel or known exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The description of a "fixed" and non-tender enlarged lymph node, combined with B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and abdominal pain, is highly concerning for a malignancy. Have you noticed any specific lumps elsewhere in your body, such as in your armpits or groin?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma
